scrotum-testes.def: The scrotum is the skin-and-muscle sac that holds the testes 2 to 3 °C below core temperature. Each testis is divided into lobules of coiled seminiferous tubules, where sperm are made, with interstitial (Leydig) cells between them that make testosterone.

male-ducts.def: The tubes that carry sperm from the testis: the epididymis, where sperm mature and are stored; the ductus (vas) deferens, which runs in the spermatic cord through the inguinal canal; and the ejaculatory duct, which opens into the urethra inside the prostate.

accessory-glands-male.def: The seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands, exocrine glands that add fluid to sperm to make semen. The seminal vesicles supply most of the volume (alkaline, with fructose); the prostate adds a milky fluid with PSA; the bulbourethral glands add mucus before ejaculation.

penis.def: The male organ that carries the urethra and delivers semen. It is made mostly of erectile tissue in three columns: two corpora cavernosa on top and a corpus spongiosum below, around the urethra, which widens into the glans penis; the prepuce (foreskin) covers the glans.

erection-ejaculation.def: Erection is the filling of erectile tissue with blood when parasympathetic nerves release nitric oxide and its smooth muscle relaxes. Ejaculation is the release of semen: sympathetic nerves move it into the urethra (emission), then a somatic reflex through the pudendal nerve expels it (expulsion).
